edge: Include one program with no initial procedure and another whose initial procedure ends; the no-initial program does not prevent implicit finish.
positive: Allow the last initial-originated thread across two programs to end and observe simulation terminate without explicit $finish.

edge: Declare `program; ; endprogram` to exercise an empty anonymous-program body item.
negative: Place an initial construct in an anonymous program body.
positive: Declare an anonymous program containing one permitted function declaration.

edge: Place an anonymous program directly in compilation-unit scope.
negative: Declare the same identifier both inside the anonymous program and elsewhere in its containing namespace.
positive: Declare an anonymous-program task in a package and call it from a program using the package namespace.

negative: From an anonymous program, hierarchically read a named program variable.
positive: Use only local declarations from an anonymous program.

edge: Call the same task from module and program threads.
positive: Call a package task from a program and observe blocking statements in Reactive.

edge: Reference through an enclosing module hierarchy while both endpoints remain program scopes.
positive: Have one named program hierarchically read a signal in another named program.

edge: Call program code from another program.
negative: Attempt to call a program-declared task from a module process.
positive: Call a module- or package-declared task from a program.

edge: Accept either presence or absence of a warning while requiring the call to be ignored.
notes: Do not require warning text or even warning issuance.
positive: Call $exit from a module initial process and verify execution continues.

edge: Follow the import with only a parameter-port list.
negative: Terminate an ANSI program header after a package import with neither parameters nor ports.
positive: Place a package import before an ANSI program port-declaration list.

edge: Clock the assertion from a program object and exercise the scheduler iteration back to Observed.
positive: Place a concurrent assertion in a program and verify it samples the preponed value and evaluates in Observed.

edge: Parse extern ANSI and non-ANSI program headers and a wildcard-port program declaration.
negative: Place a module-only body item in a program declaration.
positive: Parse named ANSI and non-ANSI programs containing permitted declarations and initial/final constructs.

edge: Keep a second initial procedure alive and verify descendants are not terminated prematurely.
positive: Fork a nonterminating descendant from a program initial block and verify it is terminated when all program initials end.

edge: Drive a design signal that feeds a program continuous assignment and observe the assignment with Reactive-region ordering.
positive: Trigger a program event control from a design-signal transition and order its action after same-time Active-region design work.

edge: Run another program concurrently and verify $exit affects only the originating program.
positive: Call $exit() in a forked descendant of one program initial and verify all initial families in that program terminate.

edge: Use an elaboration severity system task as a program generate item.
negative: Hide a program-illegal declaration inside a program generate region.
positive: Generate an allowed program declaration item under a conditional generate construct.

edge: Hierarchically refer to the implicit instance using the program declaration name.
positive: Declare an uninstantiated top-level portless program and observe its initial procedure execute once.

edge: Declare multiple program initial procedures and observe each with Reactive-region ordering.
positive: At time zero, order a program initial observation after same-time Active-region module initial activity.

edge: From one program call a subroutine in another program.
positive: From a program, call a module function and module task.

edge: Nest a portless program in an interface.
positive: Nest two programs in one module and access a variable in the enclosing module scope.

edge: Compare variable-port with resolved net-port propagation.
positive: Drive a program output net and observe a receiving module process in the next Active-region iteration.

edge: Connect program ports to design nets and variables declared in an interface scope.
negative: Attempt to instantiate a program within a program scope.
positive: Connect program ports to module variables and nets.

edge: Instantiate a program at top level with an implicit named port connection.
negative: Use a port connection form that is illegal for a module on an otherwise equivalent program instance.
positive: Instantiate a named program and connect scalar and interface ports using module-style connections.

edge: Attempt to declare another program inside a program.
negative: Place an always procedure or module instance directly in a program.
positive: Declare data, classes, subroutines, objects, and initial/final procedures in a program.

edge: Contrast simultaneous module NBA and program Re-NBA updates.
positive: Issue a program nonblocking assignment and compare its update with reactive activity.

edge: Use successive nonzero delays in a program process and verify each resumption has Reactive-region ordering.
positive: Resume a program process after a nonzero # delay and order its action after same-time Active-region design work.

edge: Use the same name in a program and an enclosing scope and verify scoped resolution.
positive: Declare program data, a task, and a function and resolve them within the program scope.

edge: Compare a program-scope variable with an automatic local variable in a program task.
positive: Modify a program-scope variable across repeated subroutine calls and observe retained state.

edge: Attempt an external reference to a program port variable.
negative: Reference a program variable hierarchically from a module process.
positive: Reference a program signal from another named program through a hierarchical path.

edge: Use the optional timeunits declaration immediately after the program header without a later repeat.
negative: Add a non-port program-item timeunits declaration that differs from the earlier declaration.
positive: Repeat an identical timeunit/timeprecision declaration as a non-port program item.
